subject.title: Memory compaction blocks main processing lane, causing unresponsive bot for 10+ minutes

question: Should OpenClaw isolate or preempt compaction and memoryFlush from the foreground session lane, or keep the current foreground-lane model with shorter timeouts and diagnostic recovery?
rationale: The source-backed bug is still present, but the durable fix changes session ordering, transcript rotation, and channel-delivery guarantees rather than one local branch.

options.title: Isolate maintenance lane
options.body: Run compaction and memoryFlush in a dedicated bounded lane or worker so foreground messages can be admitted or acknowledged without waiting on maintenance.

options.title: Make maintenance preemptible
options.body: Keep the lane model but abort and reschedule compaction or memoryFlush when foreground user messages arrive, preserving more ordering at higher scheduler complexity.

options.title: Accept timeout mitigation
options.body: Treat the current 180-second default timeout and stuck-session recovery as sufficient, leaving foreground turns blocked during active compaction windows.

recommendation.title: Isolate maintenance lane
recommendation.body: Run compaction and memoryFlush in a dedicated bounded lane or worker so foreground messages can be admitted or acknowledged without waiting on maintenance.

likelyOwner.reason: Current source blame carries the central code in this checkout, and the decision crosses the compaction and reply-lane paths attributed to that recent work.
